chunks: And he (peace be upon him) said:
Even if Allah had not threatened [with punishment] for disobedience, it would be obligatory that He not be disobeyed, as a thanksgiving for His favors.
ai.seo_question: Why is obedience to God obligatory even without the threat of punishment?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) articulates a profound theological principle in Nahj al-Balagha, distinguishing between obedience motivated by fear of punishment and that rooted in natural gratitude (shukr) for divine favors. This narration underscores the Shia scholarly view that God's commandments are inherently just and beneficial, making obedience an obligatory response to His benevolence even in the absence of eschatological threats.
